A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work and contain readable text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–D. Matching content across the tool renaming and page reflow supports a reliable comparison.

before.justification: Section 7 reports original runtime, counterexample-quality, ablation, and multifeature experiments for SViM. Appendices B and C provide generated counterexamples and Veritas comparison results.

after.justification: Section 7 and Appendices B–C report original experiments and generated counterexamples for the tool now named Ensense, including runtime and counterexample-quality results.

M1.justification: Sections 4–6 retain the same MILP optimizations, product-of-marginals objective, SMT clause synthesis, and multiclass extension. SViM is renamed Ensense without changing the procedure.

E1.justification: Tables 1–2 retain the same binary and multiclass benchmark coverage. The multifeature scenarios and Appendix B examples from IJCNN, Adult, and Pima Diabetes are also unchanged.

E2.justification: Binary comparisons retain Kant and SensPB; multiclass comparisons retain Kant and the adapted Veritas comparison in Appendix C. The data-aware variants compared in Table 3 are unchanged.

E3.justification: Both retain the 20% validation split, model configurations, gap settings, 1,290 binary and 538 multiclass instances, and filtering of subsecond runtimes. The 3,600-second main timeout and Appendix C's 1,200-second Veritas budget also remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The optimization ablations in Figure 6, data-aware component comparisons, one-to-five-feature analysis in Figure 7, and five tabular case studies in Appendix B are retained without substantive revision.

E5.justification: Both versions disclose validation-split seed 42. Neither changes repeated-run reporting or introduces error bars, confidence intervals, significance tests, or other uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Reported numerical results and findings remain unchanged. For example, Table 3 retains mean distances of 0.57, 0.306, 0.26, and 0.17 for None, Clause, Prob, and Probclause; Table 4 and Appendix B retain their values. Figure 4 redisplays the same runtime curves with altered plotting margins.

T1.justification: The sensitivity definitions, hardness results, encoding-correctness theorems, Lemma 5.2, and appendix derivations remain unchanged. Rewording the introduction to Lemma 5.2 does not alter its statement, assumptions, or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about depth-1 hardness, data-aware witnesses, multiclass sensitivity verification, scalability, and speedups. The tool renaming does not redefine the contributions.

C2.justification: Both retain the feature-independence qualification, interpretations of the ablation and multifeature results, and discussion of Veritas comparison limitations. The scope restriction to identifying counterexamples and future work on reducing sensitivity are unchanged.

D1.justification: XGBoost version, preprocessing, hyperparameter grids, solver choices, single-core execution, clause-synthesis limits, and Appendix D's worked encoding are unchanged. No code or data access information is added or removed.

R1.justification: The cited works and positioning relative to prior sensitivity and robustness verification research remain the same. No research citation or substantive novelty comparison is added or removed.

P1.justification: SViM becomes Ensense throughout, accompanied by limited grammar, punctuation, paragraph, and cross-reference edits. Author contacts and acknowledgments are updated, and Appendix C loses an editorial sentence; the overall organization is retained.

P2.justification: Figure 4 updates the tool label, moves legends, changes plotting margins, and shortens the runtime-axis label. Table 4 updates the method header, while front matter and text reflow alter page breaks. No figures or tables are added or removed.

improvement.justification: The revision mainly renames the tool and makes small editorial and display adjustments; its scientific argument, evidence, and reproducibility information remain unchanged. Modest copyediting polish, alongside less explicit runtime-axis labeling in Figure 4, produces no meaningful net change in overall quality.
